title: Ezra Bible Quiz - Chapter 9
description: Ten questions on Ezra 9: the report of mixed marriages and Ezra's prayer of confession.

questions.text: What did the princes report that the people, priests and Levites had not done?
questions.explanation: Ezra 9:1 says they had not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands.

answers.text: Kept the feast of tabernacles in its season
Paid the king's tribute on their fields
Finished building the house of their God
Separated themselves from the peoples of the lands

questions.text: Whose hand had been chief in this trespass, according to the princes?
questions.explanation: In Ezra 9:1-2 the princes say that the hand of the princes and rulers had been chief in this trespass.

questions.text: What did the narrator do when he heard this?
questions.explanation: Ezra 9:3 says, "I tore my garment and my robe, and pulled the hair out of my head and of my beard, and sat down confounded."

answers.text: Tore his garment and pulled out his hair
Went straight to the king to complain
Sent angry letters to all the princes
Built a new altar in the temple court

questions.text: Until when did the narrator sit confounded?
questions.explanation: Ezra 9:4 says, "I sat confounded until the evening offering."

questions.text: What did the narrator do at the evening offering?
questions.explanation: Ezra 9:5 says, "I fell on my knees, and spread out my hands to Yahweh my God."

answers.text: Read the law aloud to the people
Knelt and spread out his hands to Yahweh
Offered a ram for his guilt
Went into the room of the high priest

questions.text: In the prayer, what has grown up to the heavens?
questions.explanation: Ezra 9:6 says, "our guiltiness has grown up to the heavens."

questions.text: According to the prayer, what had God given them in his holy place?
questions.explanation: Ezra 9:8 says God had given them a nail in his holy place.

questions.text: In the sight of which kings had God extended loving kindness to them?
questions.explanation: Ezra 9:9 says God extended loving kindness to them in the sight of the kings of Persia.

questions.text: What had God commanded about their daughters, according to the prayer?
questions.explanation: Ezra 9:11-12 recalls what God commanded by the prophets: "don't give your daughters to their sons."

answers.text: To give them as gifts to the king
To send them back to Babylon
To make them singers in the temple
Not to give them to the sons of those peoples

questions.text: How is God addressed in the last verse of the prayer?
questions.explanation: Ezra 9:15 says, "Yahweh, the God of Israel, you are righteous."
